Marco laughed. "Dr. Calloway, you mean."
Russell laughed, too. "After four years of watching her show, it's hard not to call her Christina the Chemist. I could whistle the theme song in my sleep."

alternativeText.text: Cora sits in the passenger seat of a car, looking nervous and slightly scared as she grips her seatbelt. Her grandmother is driving, focused on the road ahead.

textContent.text: Braking at a red light, Grandma slid her eyes from the road to my face. "What's wrong, Tiana? Usually, you can't wait to see Cousin Justine."
I sighed. "I know."
Grandma just waited, and I sighed again. "Justine's so…brave," I mumbled.
"So are you."

"I could never be as brave as she is." It was true. One week my cousin was whooshing down a hundred-foot water slide, and the next week she was swinging on a trapeze. And every time, I got a text saying, "Tiana, you HAVE to try this."

Yesterday, Justine had posted videos of herself skateboarding. Not just skateboarding, of course, but doing stunts, too. Daredevil stuff. I'd only ever tried skateboarding once, and it had left me with a chipped front tooth. No way was I going to try that again.
"Bravery comes in many forms," Grandma declared.
"Right," I said glumly.

contents.text: Maya's face turned red, and she ducked her head.
"Did—did everyone see that?" Maya stuttered.
People often blush and stutter when they're embarrassed. Either of these sentences would help show the reader how Maya is feeling.
